brief: Frontier AI labs publicly backed pacing advanced model development over the weekend, following closed-door talks to form an industry safety standards body. Departing alignment researchers had warned advanced AI could threaten human survival. AI-linked stocks fell Monday: North Asian memory names down 2.9-6.4%, SoftBank down 10.7%. A bipartisan US Senate AI-rules effort is progressing and California enacted independent-AI-auditor standards. Trump opposed a slowdown, calling US AI leadership a priority. UBS argues pacing does not imply lower capex. Inference, roughly two-thirds of compute demand, is driven by real-world adoption and monetization, not model-capability pacing, and training continues (Musk confirmed ongoing Grok 4.8 training, OpenAI reiterated growth in memory demand), so UBS keeps its 2027 AI capex forecast at USD 1.2tr, up 33% from an estimated USD 900bn this year. Regulation may reshape competition rather than slow development, favoring larger incumbents and raising barriers for startups and non-compliant overseas rivals. Valuations have already de-rated (SOXX at 21x forward earnings versus 33x in June). UBS says the real question is whether AI demand keeps expanding, believes yes, and favors diversified AI-value-chain exposure over concentrated positions.
